item.title: Harden ledger concurrency tests and validation bypass
item.brief: Follow-up to the ledger.py work on this branch. Make the test suite fail rather than hang on a concurrency regression: give every thread join a timeout and assert the thread finished. Make test_snapshots_never_see_a_half_transfer fail if its writer thread raises, by collecting thread exceptions and re-raising them in the test. Make the validation in ledger.py not depend on a dict subclass overriding items(): read the ledger's balances through a plain-dict copy or direct iteration that the validation cannot be bypassed through. Keep the change small, keep all tests passing, and keep the standard library only. Commit on the item's branch with a clear message and no attribution lines.

pr.title: Harden ledger validation and concurrency tests

agt_01M88YW5PSWN6GMBXXN9PKC9M2:1.description: test_snapshots_never_see_a_half_transfer polls done.is_set() in an unbounded loop that also calls ledger.snapshot() (which needs the same lock). If the writer thread deadlocks, the main thread spins or blocks forever before _join_or_fail runs, so the test hangs instead of failing as the intent requires. at test_ledger.py:187

agt_01M88YW5PSWN6GMBXXN9PKC9M2:2.description: Invariant checks in _transfer_locked are bare assert statements; they are stripped under python -O, so production correctness checks depend on interpreter flags. at ledger.py:59

agt_01M88YW5PSWN6GMBXXN9PKC9M2:3.description: The snapshot test only detects half-transfers probabilistically: if the writer finishes before the main loop observes intermediate states, it passes trivially. A deterministic check (e.g., a barrier or a snapshot count floor) would make the test stronger. at test_ledger.py:168

risk.why: Touches ledger.py constructor validation (behaviour change: dict subclasses with lying items() are now handled correctly) and concurrency tests. No lock or transfer logic changed. Reviewers rated low (test-only delta) but the validation change is in shipped code, so kept medium. Review 1 found one blocking hang risk, fixed and re-reviewed.

item.title: Implement ledger.py per SPEC.md with tests
item.brief: Implement `ledger.py` in the repository root according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API exactly, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests covering them (the existing tests cover basics only; extend them, do not delete them). Use the Python standard library only. Read SPEC.md first and treat it as the source of truth. Run the test suite before finishing and make sure it passes. Commit the work on the item's branch with a clear message; do not add attribution lines to the commit.

pr.body: Approach: one threading.Lock per Ledger; every read and write happens under it, so transfers are linearizable and opposite transfers cannot deadlock. Amount is validated before account lookup; unknown accounts raise KeyError; insufficient funds and destination overflow return False with no change; same-account transfers return True iff funded and never change balances. Key files: ledger.py, test_ledger.py (original 2 tests kept). Checks: python3 -m unittest, 22 OK. Reviewer agt_01M88YQGD83GV0X5FMKMHSEJD7 passed the head with no blocking findings. Non-blocking follow-ups: (1) test_snapshots_never_see_a_half_transfer does not fail if the writer thread raises; (2) concurrency tests could hang rather than fail if a deadlock regresses; (3) validation uses items() so a dict subclass overriding items() could be copied unvalidated; spec says 'a dict', so not a violation.
pr.summary: Made Ledger(balances), transfer() and snapshot() work per SPEC.md. Now atomic and thread-safe via one lock per ledger. Before: all methods raised NotImplementedError (2 test errors). Now: 22 tests pass.
pr.title: Implement atomic Ledger per SPEC.md with tests

agt_01M88YQGD83GV0X5FMKMHSEJD7:1.description: test_snapshots_never_see_a_half_transfer swallows worker exceptions: the worker's finally only sets done, so a transfer that raises (e.g. KeyError or ValueError) stops the loop early and the test still passes, since every observed total is still 1500.

agt_01M88YQGD83GV0X5FMKMHSEJD7:2.description: Concurrency tests can hang rather than fail if a deadlock regresses. In test_snapshots, the main thread's snapshot() blocks on the same lock the stuck worker holds, so there is no timeout. In test_opposite_transfers the threads are non-daemon, so a stuck thread can keep the interpreter alive after the assertion fails.

agt_01M88YQGD83GV0X5FMKMHSEJD7:3.description: JOIN_SECONDS uses wall-clock timeouts for deadlock detection. SPEC.md says tests use no wall-clock calculations; I read this as allowing timeouts but not timing-derived expectations. The 2 s budget is generous for about 2000 in-memory transfers, but this is a possible spec-wording conflict.

agt_01M88YQGD83GV0X5FMKMHSEJD7:4.description: Constructor validates via balances.items() and then copies with dict(balances). For a dict subclass that overrides items() or __iter__, the validated pairs and the copied contents can differ. The spec says 'a dict', so this is an edge case and not a spec violation as written.
